overview_pre: This page is a **compendium of less common lumps** (each covered in a short section below), rather than one disease.
kf: Lumps here: **neurofibroma** (soft, 'buttonhole' sign; many = NF1), **pilomatricoma** (rock-hard, children), **digital myxoid cyst** (near the nail, osteoarthritis), sebaceous hyperplasia, connective tissue naevi and others.
Six or more café-au-lait macules ≥5 mm (prepubertal) or ≥15 mm (adults) plus neurofibromas or freckling: **NF1**.
Rapid growth, pain, size over 5 cm or deep location: think sarcoma, refer urgently.
Most are benign: reassure, excise if symptomatic or uncertain.
Use ultrasound when the depth or nature is unclear.
myths: **"A hard lump is always cancer"**: pilomatricoma is rock-hard but benign.
comp: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour in plexiform neurofibromas (NF1); recurrence after excision.
